insights.headline: Gold imports plunge 81% to a 30-month low as policy rationing bites; Fed-hike bets pin bullion
insights.summary: Commerce Ministry data showed September gold imports down 81.3% year-on-year to $1.8 billion — a 30-month low — as the May duty hike and SEBI's gold fund-of-funds freeze ration demand ahead of Diwali. Hot US inflation (CPI 3.7%, PPI +6.3%) kept Fed-hike expectations elevated and capped gold near $4,145–4,195; silver, down more than half from January's $121.79 record, flashed slowdown warnings even as solar-cell makers barely passed on its slide since August.
points: September gold imports fell 81.3% YoY to $1.8B, a 30-month low; the $7.8B drop in the gold bill narrowed the trade deficit to $30.2B.
US September CPI 3.7% YoY (vs 3.6% forecast), PPI +6.3% YoY; experts see gold at ₹1.60 lakh/10g and silver at ₹2.40 lakh/kg by end-2026.
Silver fell from its $121.79 January record to $57.31, down more than half; gold is off over 25% from its $5,626.80 January record.
SEBI barred fresh lump-sum, SIP and STP flows into gold fund-of-funds from October 16; gold ETFs are untouched and existing SIPs continue.
RHB stays short COMEX gold from $4,284.80 (stop-loss $4,400) and warns of $4,000, then $3,800, if $4,200 resistance fails.

trending.title: Policy is rationing gold before Diwali
trending.summary: SEBI froze gold fund-of-funds investments from October 16 while leaving gold ETFs open — a gap experts say investors can bypass — and September imports hit a 30-month low after the May duty hike.

trending.title: Hot US inflation keeps the Fed-hike trade alive
trending.summary: September CPI at 3.7% and PPI up 6.3% year-on-year revived rate-hike bets; gold held near $4,145–4,195 while RHB warned a failed $4,200 breakout could drag COMEX gold toward $4,000.

trending.title: Silver's slide is macro and industrial at once
trending.summary: Silver has lost more than half its value since January's $121.79 record, flashing slowdown warnings; SMM notes a separate ~20% slide since late August that solar cell prices have barely followed.

items.title: Gold imports plunge 81% to 30-month low; ICRA sees CAD widening to 0.9% of GDP
items.summary: India's gold imports plunged 81.3% year-on-year to $1.8 billion in September — the lowest in 30 months — helping narrow the merchandise trade deficit to $30.2 billion from $33 billion, Commerce Ministry data showed. The $7.8 billion drop in the gold bill more than offset higher oil and electronics imports. ICRA said the easing was non-oil driven and forecast the CAD at 0.9% of GDP in FY27.

items.title: US Fed rate hike buzz: American inflation highest since COVID — what does it mean for Nifty, Sensex, gold rates?
items.summary: US producer prices rose the most in 4-1/2 years in September and CPI accelerated to 3.7% year-on-year — the hottest American inflation since COVID — fueling rate-hike buzz ahead of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting. Market experts told Mint that Dalal Street has already discounted hikes through December, and they predict gold at ₹1.60 lakh per 10 grams and silver at ₹2.40 lakh per kg by end-2026.

items.title: Silver's recent 50% drop from a record high hints that an economic slowdown looms
items.summary: Silver futures touched a record intraday $121.79 an ounce in late January, per Dow Jones Market Data, and have since lost more than half, settling at $57.31 on Friday. Dealers told MarketWatch that silver's dual monetary-industrial role makes its weakness a leading indicator of economic trouble as high energy prices bite. Gold has fallen more than 25% from its own January record of $5,626.80.

items.title: Sebi's gold fund curbs may have limited impact as ETF route remains open
items.summary: SEBI has asked mutual funds to stop fresh lump-sum, SIP and STP investments into gold ETF fund-of-funds from October 16, aiming to curb gold demand and ease rupee pressure — but the curbs don't touch gold ETFs themselves. Mint reports experts warning that investors can simply buy ETFs directly on exchanges with a demat account, which could defeat the purpose. Existing SIPs continue as usual.

items.title: India Bullion: Up on weak dollar; market assesses Fed rate outlook
items.summary: MCX December gold rose 0.6% to ₹1,48,320 per 10 grams and December silver gained 1.4% to ₹2,13,570 per kg on Friday as the dollar index fell to a two-week low of 101.57; COMEX gold was up 0.6% at $4,195.3 and silver up 1.5% at $57.99. Kotak Securities cited safe-haven flows from the equity selloff, while Commerzbank said Fed Chair Warsh's comments further dented October hike expectations.

items.title: Bullion Cues: Weakness may deepen
items.summary: Gold ($4,165.40) and silver ($57) lost 0.7% and 6.3% last week; MCX gold futures (₹1,47,918) fell 2.4% and silver (₹2,11,187) 6.5%. The Hindu BusinessLine's research bureau says MCX gold must cross ₹1,51,700 to turn positive, with supports at ₹1,43,500 and ₹1,41,000; silver could slide to the ₹2,00,000–2,00,750 band unless it reclaims ₹2,28,000–2,30,000.

items.title: [SMM Analysis] Silver Down Nearly 20% From Stage High: Why Are Solar Cell Prices Not Following?
items.summary: SMM's #1 silver price fell 19.6% from its August 27 high of 16,889 yuan/kg to 13,584 yuan/kg on October 15, edging to 13,842 yuan/kg on the 16th. Yet solar cell prices barely budged: M10 cell costs fell 10.8% to 0.310 yuan/W while G12R prices held flat since September 18. SMM blames hawkish Fed minutes, a dollar index above 102 and multi-year-high yields; COMEX silver broke below $60 on October 8.

items.title: Selling Pressure Resumption Could Push Gold To US$4,000, Says RHB
items.summary: RHB Research kept its bearish call on COMEX gold despite Thursday's rebound to a $4,170.10 close, calling it a countertrend bounce with the RSI still below 50. The house advises holding shorts initiated September 23 at $4,284.80 with a $4,400 stop-loss; a failure to clear $4,200 resistance could renew selling toward $4,000 and then $3,800. RHB stays negative unless gold moves above $4,400.

items.title: Peter Schiff: Gold Should Have Soared This Week... Traders Just Handed You a Gift
items.summary: Three hot US inflation prints in three days — CPI at 3.7% year-on-year, PPI up 6.3% annually, import prices up 1.1% — pushed gold down about 0.6% on the week as traders priced more Fed hikes. Peter Schiff argued on X on October 17 that the selloff means the Fed has already lost its inflation fight, calling gold at $4,145 ‘a gift’; his podcast put silver near $56.85 as a buying opportunity.

items.title: US Dollar Heads For Weekly Loss As AI Selloff Shifts Rate Outlook
items.summary: The dollar fell on Friday, on track for its first weekly decline in over a month against the euro and yen, as fading Fed rate-hike expectations and an AI-driven equity selloff weighed. The dollar index slipped 0.25% to 101.77, set for a 0.45% weekly drop. Cautious Fed remarks tempered October hike bets — markets assigned an 87% probability to a hold, per CME FedWatch.
